bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 255 in `ot::Mle::Mle::HandleParentResponse`. The staged 38-byte `radio-receive-done` witness reaches the MLE Parent Response parser; the saved bytes contain `0a 04 ff`, and on the reproduced path `HandleUdpReceive` dispatches command `0x0a` (`kCommandParentResponse`) before `HandleParentResponse` parses a `Response` TLV whose copied header length is 255. `Tlv::GetTlv(aMessage, Tlv::kResponse, sizeof(response), response)` copies only `sizeof(ResponseTlv) == 10` bytes into stack local `ResponseTlv response` but preserves the advertised length 255 in the copied header. `response.IsValid()` still accepts that object because it only checks for a lower bound of 8 bytes. The subsequent `memcmp(response.GetResponse(), mParentRequest.mChallenge, response.GetLength())` reuses the attacker-controlled length 255 even though both compared fields are fixed 8-byte arrays, so `memcmp()` reads past stack local `response`. The patch resolves the bug by clamping uses of the field length with the new `ResponseTlv::GetResponseLength()` helper and replacing the vulnerable `response.GetLength()` compare bound.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the malformed Response TLV on the crashing path. This statement copies the attacker-controlled Response TLV into fixed stack local `response` that is later over-read by `memcmp()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 38 bytes and contains `0a 04 ff` at offsets 23-25. On the reproduced path `HandleUdpReceive` reads command byte `0x0a` and dispatches to `HandleParentResponse`; the next parsed TLV is therefore type `kResponse` with advertised length `0xff` (255) when line 3214 copies it into `response`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This parse preserves the attacker-controlled Response TLV header length 255 inside stack local `response` even though `ot::Tlv::Get()` only copies `sizeof(response) == 10` bytes total.

root_cause.description: The compare bound comes directly from the attacker-controlled TLV header instead of the fixed 8-byte `ResponseTlv::mResponse` field size. The patch replaces this bound with `response.GetResponseLength()`.
root_cause.note: Because step 1 preserved header length 255 in `response`, this expression yields 255 even though the copied `ResponseTlv` only holds the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte response field. Reusing the raw TLV length here is the missing size obligation that makes the later `memcmp()` unsafe.

sink.description: ASan sink. `memcmp()` uses the attacker-controlled bound 255 while its first operand is the fixed 8-byte response field inside stack local `response`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 255` at `mle.cpp:3215:5` through `bcmp` and identifies stack object `response` at line 3192 as `[32,42)` in the crashing frame. `response.GetResponse()` starts at the object's 8-byte value field, so this compare reads past the end of `response` and into adjacent stack locals.

parser_admitted.description: The MLE receive path has already accepted the packet as an allowed MLE command, read command byte `0x0a` (`kCommandParentResponse`), and dispatched into the vulnerable Parent Response parser.

fine_trace.note: Source. This parses the Parent Response message's `Response` TLV into stack local `response`. With the staged witness's copied TLV header length `0xff`, `ot::Tlv::Get()` first reads the TLV header, sees `GetLength() == 255`, and then re-reads only `sizeof(response) == 10` bytes because that is the caller's maximum. The resulting `response` object therefore keeps header length 255 but contains only the 2-byte TLV header plus the fixed 8-byte `mResponse` field.

The validation gate still admits the malformed TLV. `ResponseTlv::IsValid()` only requires `GetLength() >= sizeof(*this) - sizeof(Tlv)`, which is 8, so the copied header length 255 passes and the short-circuit expression continues toward `memcmp()` instead of rejecting the oversized length.

Root cause. The compare size is taken directly from the copied TLV header, so this expression yields 255 rather than the fixed 8-byte extent of `ResponseTlv::mResponse`. The patch replaces this raw length with `response.GetResponseLength()`, which clamps the bound to `sizeof(mResponse)`.

ASan sink. `response.GetResponse()` points at the fixed 8-byte `mResponse` array inside stack object `response`, while `mParentRequest.mChallenge` is also a fixed 8-byte array. Using the attacker-controlled size 255 from step 3 makes `memcmp()` read beyond the end of `response`; the saved ASan report records `READ of size 255` and names `response` `[32,42)` as the overrun stack object.

format.contract: Exact staged 38-byte radio-frame witness. On the reproduced path `HandleUdpReceive` reads command byte `0x0a` (`kCommandParentResponse`), and the subsequent bytes parsed as the `Response` TLV header are `04 ff`, so `HandleParentResponse` copies a `ResponseTlv` whose stored length is 255 into fixed stack local `response`. This exact file is the only verified trigger artifact here; Stage 02 does not generalize to a wider range of frames or lengths.
